Class ByteReader

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.core.io.ByteReader
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, AutoCloseable
public final class ByteReader extends Object implements Closeable
Reads a stream of bytes: numbers in either byte order, runs of bytes, text and lines, with lookahead and search.

A reader holds a buffer, and reads from its stream only when a call needs bytes that aren't buffered yet, taking what the stream has at hand: it never waits for more bytes than the call needs, so it works on sockets and pipes.

Methods that read a number read it in big-endian order, as DataInputStream does; those whose name ends in Le read it in little-endian order.

When the stream ends before a read method has all the bytes it needs, the method throws EOFException and leaves the reader at the end of the stream. The lookahead methods, request(int), require(int), exhausted(), peek(), startsWith(Bytes) and the indexOf methods, never consume anything. 

try (var in = ByteSource.of(classFile).openReader()) {
    if (in.readInt() != 0xCAFEBABE) {
        throw new IOException("not a class file: " + classFile);
    }
    var minor = in.readUnsignedShort();
    var major = in.readUnsignedShort();
}

A reader owns its stream: close() closes it, and any other call that needs the stream after that throws IOException. A reader is not safe for use by several threads at once.

Since:
0.2.0

    • readLine

      public Optional<String> readLine(int maxBytes, Charset charset) throws IOException
      Reads a line of text encoded in a charset. A line ends with a line feed (\n), a carriage return (\r), a carriage return followed by a line feed, or the end of the stream, as for BufferedReader.readLine(). Malformed input is replaced as by String(byte[], Charset).

      Only charsets that encode both terminators as single bytes, as ASCII does, can be read this way, such as UTF-8 or ISO-8859-1. Lines in other charsets, such as UTF-16, can be read with CharReader.

      Parameters:
      maxBytes - the number of bytes the line may have, at most, its terminator excluded
      charset - the charset the text is encoded in
      Returns:
      the line, without its terminator, or an empty optional at the end of the stream
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if maxBytes is negative, or if charset doesn't encode the line terminators as ASCII does
      IOException - if the line has more than maxBytes bytes, in which case nothing is consumed, or if the stream cannot be read
